question: For the unchanged actual strong cycle input, does local response error arise under time-varying mean alone, time-varying variances alone, or only their joint time dependence?
counterfactuals: full is unchanged. mean_only keeps the original mean waveform and replaces each raw variance-intensity waveform with its own time average. variances_only keeps both original variance waveforms and fixes the mean at its own time average. Original group threshold and source period retained.
prediction: No fit: same voltage-corrected response tables, poles and static spline as existing nonlinear_mean_readout diagnostics. All 12 predictions locked before new targets; full-input binned predictions must reproduce saved references.
statistical_unit: Independent noise path; common random numbers pair the 12 input conditions. Three conditions per source population are paired counterfactual assays, not independent biological replicates.
budget: One preparation, one 12-condition local LIF batch and independent readout audit. No coefficient fitting, network launches or bifurcation scans.
trigger: The fresh bounded-input assay passed all 12 conditions for both closures. This follow-up retains original strong amplitudes while separating time-dependent mean and variance input.
scope: Local strong-input diagnostic, not an autonomous reduced network or native SNN validation. Full-input condition repeats a previously seen waveform with new noise; eight channel-clamped waveforms have new targets. A conditional failure identifies an input context, not by itself the unique correct closure or onset bifurcation.
